verses.gurmukhi: ਅੰਨ੍ਹੇ ਅਗੇ ਆਰਸੀ ਨਾਈ ਧਰਿ ਨ ਵਧਾਈ ਪਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: a(n)nhe age aarasee naiee dhar na vadhaiee paavai|

en.bdb: A barber showing mirror to a blind person never gets the reward.

verses.gurmukhi: ਬੋਲੇ ਅਗੇ ਗਾਵੀਐ ਸੂੰਮ ਨ ਡੂਮ ਕਵਾਇ ਪੈਨ੍ਹਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: bole age gaaveeaai soo(n)m na ddoom kavai painhaavai|

en.bdb: Singing before a deaf person is in vain and likewise a miser does not present a robe to his minstrel as a gift.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪੁਛੈ ਮਸਲਤਿ ਗੁੰਗਿਅਹੁ ਵਿਗੜੈ ਕੰਮੁ ਜਵਾਬੁ ਨ ਆਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: puchhai masalat gu(n)giahu vigaRai ka(n)m javaab na aavai|

en.bdb: If the dumb is consulted on any issue, the issue will go worse and he will not be able to answer.

verses.gurmukhi: ਫੁਲਵਾੜੀ ਵੜਿ ਗੁਣਗੁਣਾ ਮਾਲੀ ਨੋ ਨ ਇਨਾਮੁ ਦਿਵਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: fulavaaRee vaR gunagunaa maalee no na inaam dhivaavai|

en.bdb: If a person devoid of the sense of smell goes to a garden, he cannot recommend the gardener for award.

verses.gurmukhi: ਲੂਲੇ ਨਾਲਿ ਵਿਆਹੀਐ ਕਿਵ ਗਲਿ ਮਿਲਿ ਕਾਮਣਿ ਗਲਿ ਲਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: loole naal viaaheeaai kiv gal mil kaaman gal laavai|

en.bdb: How could a woman married to a cripple embrace him.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਭਨਾ ਚਾਲ ਸੁਹਾਵਣੀ ਲੰਗੜਾ ਕਰੇ ਲਖਾਉ ਲੰਗਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: sabhanaa chaal suhaavanee la(n)gaRaa kare lakhaau la(n)gaavai|

en.bdb: Where all others have a fair gait, the lame however he may pretend, would definitely be seen limping.
Thus, the fool never remains hidden, and he definitely exposes himself.
